description_full: Zensho Holdings Co., Ltd. engages in the management of food service chain restaurants, and development of sales systems and food processing systems in Japan, the United States, China, Europe, ASEAN, and internationally. It operates through Global Sukiya, Global Hama Sushi, Global Prepared Food, Global Fast Food, Restaurants, Retail, Head Office and Support, and Other segments. The company's restaurants offer gyudon, udon, tempura, shabu-shabu, hamburger steaks, pasta, noodles, desserts, and drinks, as well as provides conveyor-belt sushi restaurant, coffee shop, and dining services under the Sukiya, Nakau, Coco's, Big Boy, Victoria Station, Jolly Pasta, EI Torito, Hama-sushi, Hanaya Yohei, Denmaru, Kyubeiya, Jukusei Yakiniku Ichiban, Katsu-An, and Olive Hill brands. It also operates Chicken Rice Shop, as well as sells products under AFC, ZENSHI, SNOWFOX, SNOWFRUIT, Bento, YO!, Taiko, SushiTake, and Sushi Circle brands. In addition, the company operates supermarket chains under Joy Foods, United Veggies, Maruya, Attack, Fujimart, Maruei, and Very Foods Owariya brand names; and offers residential and nursing care services for the elderly under Kagayaki, Royalhouse Ishioka, Enju, NYEREG, and IMedicare brand names. Further, it engages in the manufacturing and processing of food ingredients; logistics; store equipment installation and maintenance; uniforms, and other related items under GFF, Zensho Shoji, Global Fresh Supply, Techno Construction, and Global Table Supply brands. The company was formerly known as Zensho Co., Ltd. and changed its name to Zensho Holdings Co., Ltd. in October 2011. Zensho Holdings Co., Ltd. was incorporated in 1982 and is headquartered in Tokyo, Japan.

financial_summary: ZENSHO HLDGS CO LTD is a large-cap consumer cyclical business with a $12.6B market cap on $7.9B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +13% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 9% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically. Gross margins of 54% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $130M in free cash flow — roughly 2 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.21× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.9× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 11.6×.

Net dilution runs at 1.7% annually, transferring value from owners to stock-based comp, and insiders hold 40% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
